---
title: "Install R (and optionally Python)"
---

The course is taught in **R**: install it first. The exercises also show every code
example and solution in **Python**, so if you prefer Python you can work the
exercises in it; install it as well in that case.

## R

1. Install a recent [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) (4.3 or newer) from CRAN.
2. We recommend [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) as editor.
3. Install the packages used in the course:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse",   # data wrangling and plotting
  "Matrix",      # dense and sparse matrices
  "deSolve",     # ordinary differential equations
  "pracma"       # textbook numerical methods (for comparison)
  # ... add packages here as the material is written
))
```

## Python (optional)

1. Install Python 3.11 or newer, e.g. via [Miniforge](https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge).
2. Any editor works; [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) and
   [JupyterLab](https://jupyter.org/) are common choices.
3. Install the packages used in the course:

```bash
pip install numpy scipy matplotlib pandas
# ... add packages here as the material is written
```

## Check it works

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```r
A <- matrix(c(2, 1, 1, 3), nrow = 2)
b <- c(1, 2)
solve(A, b)          # should print 0.2 0.6
0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3     # FALSE: see How computers store numbers
```

### Python

```python
import numpy as np
A = np.array([[2.0, 1.0], [1.0, 3.0]])
b = np.array([1.0, 2.0])
print(np.linalg.solve(A, b))   # should print [0.2 0.6]
print(0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3)        # False: see How computers store numbers
```

:::

If that prints without error, you are ready for the course!
